Sample.evidence_source: The present study was undertaken to examine whether conversations about weight loss/dieting and exercise differentially predicted body appreciation. Key to our study was the proposed mediational model whereby we examined whether the object–process dichotomy was responsible for the relationships between conversation topic and body image. Our results supported our hypotheses, and three findings are noteworthy. First, we began by showing that our sample of undergraduate women endorsed a stronger body-as-object orientation than they did a body-as-process orientation.

section_summary.extract_value: This discussion section summarizes the findings of 'the present study', which investigated how conversations about weight loss/dieting and exercise predict body appreciation, mediated by body attitudes and orientation. The study found that exercise talk predicted increased body appreciation, while weight loss/dieting talk predicted decreased appreciation, with these relationships mediated by object-process attitudes and orientation. The sample consisted of undergraduate women, and limitations regarding generalizability, measures (including the BES scale for body orientation), and causal direction were discussed.
